quizName:
Hardest Questions in South dakota
									  					
									  														  					Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness, and harms your judgment—just like drugs and alcohol.

questions.question: All vehicles must have liability insurance:

options.text: Only when a minor is driving.

questions.explanation: South Dakota law requires all vehicles to be registered and insured at all times. You must keep proof of insurance in your vehicle.

questions.question: This sign warns of a:
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers about upcoming hazards. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings.

questions.question: Children age 12 and under should ride in:
questions.explanation: Airbags can injure children. Anyone age 12 or under should sit in the back seat where airbags are located.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: When you meet an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to get out of their way. Do not compete with other drivers. Follow the rules and be respectful to all road users.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns of curves ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is slippery and dangerous. This sign warns you to slow down because your car needs more distance to stop on wet roads.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. You must stop for pedestrians, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: If you have an argument with another person and feel angry, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly while driving so you don't think about the argument.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions make it harder to drive safely. If you are very angry, excited, scared, or worried, you need time to calm down before you drive. You must focus your mind on driving, not on what upset you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to places where animals, people, and vehicles may cross the road.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or let another driver take over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let another driver take over.
questions.explanation: When you feel tired, stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, which makes driving dangerous.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means you must stop.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When you feel tired while driving, go to the nearest rest stop to take a break, nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not good replacements for rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws and must be followed. This sign means you cannot turn right where it is posted.

questions.question: When you reach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the crossing gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning devices, or flaggers warn you that a train is coming. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and roads where drivers are not allowed to enter. You may see it if you try to enter an expressway ramp going the wrong way.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.
Continue driving when you think most children have exited the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When you approach a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until the stop arm goes up and the lights turn off.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is a traffic rule. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Use your horn to get other cars to notice you.
Get out and flag down the next passing vehicle.
Pull to the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your car if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your car if possible.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if you can. Traffic on interstate highways moves very fast, which makes it dangerous to stand or walk along the side.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed. You cannot turn right at an intersection with this sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round sign always means a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: In South Dakota, who must wear safety belts in a moving vehicle?

options.text: The driver, front seat passengers, and children

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver, front seat passengers, and children
questions.explanation: The law requires the driver, all front seat passengers, and children under 18 to wear safety belts while the vehicle is moving. Young children should sit in the back seat.
